title: Petra and the Portrait Anew
premise: Felix Okonkwo, an insurance investigator with a photographic memory, is hired by a nervous client to prove a murder has not yet happened — a portrait of town benefactor Edmund Vane is scheduled to be unveiled 'anew' at the centenary gala, and the client insists someone will die the night it hangs. As Felix investigates, they discover the painting conceals a ledger of bribes and forged identities that has quietly governed the town for decades, and that the 'future' murder is actually a twenty-year-old killing the town chose to forget — one Felix's perfect memory recorded and misfiled. The client is the presumed-dead victim's child, returned to force the town to look at what it buried, and the true killer is the beloved archivist who taught Felix to file secrets away. At the gala, Felix restores the original portrait over the forgery, exposing the ledger and forcing a public reckoning that costs them their belonging in the town but returns their own name to them.
about_author: P. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing municipal archives in a small river town before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about what institutions remember and what they pay never to recall.

chapters.title: Payment in Advance
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A hooded client leaves a full fee in cash with one instruction: prove the murder hasn't happened yet. Felix's memory replays every detail of the encounter, unsettled by the client's familiar cadence. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into unease.

chapters.title: The Town That Files Itself
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Establishing the town of Harrow's Bend, its centenary preparations, and the unveiling of a restored portrait of Edmund Vane. Felix catalogs the gala committee's small evasions. Emotional beat: affection for a town Felix knows is hiding something.

chapters.title: An Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with flashback. Twenty years ago, Felix's mentor, archivist Marguerite Hale, taught them to index the town's paper life. Felix recalls one file that was never indexed — pulled before filing. Emotional beat: nostalgia shadowed by a first crack of doubt.

chapters.title: The Client's Voice
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Cross-referencing the client's speech patterns against memory, Felix narrows the match to someone connected to the Vane estate — and to a woman, Ada Okoye, listed as deceased in 2005. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt turning personal.

chapters.title: Portrait of a Benefactor
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada, alive and disguised as a conservator hired to clean the Vane portrait, examines the canvas and finds it is a forgery painted over something. Emotional beat: grief hardened into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Varnish Hides
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Under raking light, faint gridlines appear beneath the paint — columns of figures. Ada photographs them, knowing Felix will eventually be pointed her way. Emotional beat: fear braided with resolve.

chapters.title: The Murder That Hasn't Happened
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix reconstructs the 'future' murder from the client's phrasing and realizes every detail matches the 2005 disappearance of Ada's father, Samuel Okoye — ruled accidental. Emotional beat: vertigo as future and past collapse into one.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Perfect System
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix visits Marguerite, now revered town historian, to ask about the unindexed file. Marguerite deflects with warmth and a warning about digging up centenary season. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against suspicion.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada deciphers the gridlines: payments, dates, initials — including MO, Marguerite Okoye-Hale, Samuel's widow, who remarried and buried her name. Emotional beat: betrayal arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: Two Investigators, One Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Felix and Ada, each suspecting the other, meet at the conservation studio. Recognition, accusation, then alliance: the murder 'yet to happen' is the town's plan to kill the truth again. Emotional beat: wary partnership forged.

chapters.title: The Committee of Benefactors
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix traces the ledger's initials to a standing committee of five families whose 'donations' bought zoning, silence, and elections. Two signatories still live: Marguerite and councilman Rufus Vane. Emotional beat: the scale of corruption sinking in.

chapters.title: A Threat, Neatly Filed
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada's studio is ransacked; the photographs are gone, but the forgery is left slashed — a message. She realizes the conservator contract was bait to draw her out. Emotional beat: hunted, and more determined.

chapters.title: Rufus Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Rufus's POV. Rufus offers Felix a partnership: bury the ledger, share the estate's legitimacy. He reveals Marguerite has been feeding him Felix's file requests. Emotional beat: the seductive weight of offered power.

chapters.title: What Felix Forgot on Purpose
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A memory surfaces Felix has never indexed: the night Samuel Okoye died, Felix saw Marguerite at the boathouse and chose, at her request, to misfile it. Emotional beat: shame — the investigator was the town's first accomplice.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Archive
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix confronts Marguerite. She admits the ledger, claims she protected the town from ruin, and warns that exposure will destroy Ada, the Okoye name, and Felix's place here. Emotional beat: love and manipulation indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Restoration
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada and Felix plan to repaint the truth: strip the forgery during the gala unveiling and reveal the original canvas — Samuel Okoye's portrait, which Marguerite painted over, ledger and all. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Centenary Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sabotage everywhere: the gala moved up, the studio sealed, Felix's credentials revoked by Rufus's influence. Marguerite, cornered, burns the archive's original index. Emotional beat: the noose tightening.

chapters.title: The Unveiling
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the gala, the forged Vane portrait is unveiled to applause. Ada steps forward with the solvent; Felix blocks security with a recitation of the ledger, initials and sums, from memory, before the whole town. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into testimony.

chapters.title: Every Name, Aloud
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix reads the ledger publicly, ending with Samuel Okoye's name and the date of his death. The crowd turns; Rufus is taken; Marguerite stands unmoving, almost relieved. Emotional beat: catharsis with a cost.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Confession
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite confesses: Samuel discovered the ledger and threatened to end the system she believed held the town together; his death was an accident she chose to curate. She asks Felix to file her truthfully. Emotional beat: ruin and release.

chapters.title: The Portrait Anew
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Samuel Okoye's true portrait is restored and hung in the town hall; the ledger enters the public record. Ada chooses to stay, reclaiming her father's name and her own. Emotional beat: belonging, finally earned rather than granted.

chapters.title: A New Index
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix resigns from insurance work and opens an honest archive, re-indexing the town's secrets in the open. A new client arrives with a strange request — and this time, Felix files nothing away. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace.
